title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a short fragment, numbered 11, and it is entirely struck through with two diagonal strokes. It continues page 10, where Grothendieck lists equivalent conditions, under a 'divisibility' hypothesis on the ambient class 𝒜, for a refinement G of a decomposition F to deserve the name 'subdivision'.

The setup, in modern terms:
- F and G are decompositions (stratifications) of a space or 'figure' into open strata.
- Each decomposition is indexed by a set carrying an order. The order is presumably the closure or incidence order X ≤ X' ⟺ X ⊂ closure(X').
- On page 10 the conditions include: (iv) no element x ≪ F (x in Ouv(F)) is 'disjoint' (|0|) from G; and (v) G is maximal among refinements of F ordered by ⊂.
- A crossed-out condition there says the Alexandrov topology of the stratum poset F̃ is the quotient of that of G̃: X ≤ X' iff there are Y ∈ φ⁻¹(X) and Y' ∈ φ⁻¹(X') with Y ≤ Y'.

This page starts to paraphrase what being a subdivision means informally, apparently specialised to the case 𝒜 = Fig(Euc) (figures in Euclidean space), announced at the bottom of page 10. Roughly: F is obtained from G merely by 'grouping terms'. The open strata Y_j^0 of the coarse decomposition are unions of the strata X_i^0 of the finer one, 'sans plus' (nothing more). Moreover, the order on the index set, which determines the 'other forms' (presumably the non-open or closed strata), is obtained simply from the other index set's order by grouping or partition.

So it is the familiar statement that a subdivision is a refinement whose stratum poset maps onto the coarse poset as a poset quotient, with the coarse incidence relation induced by the fine one. The passage was abandoned (struck out and unfinished); it is the last page of the file and there is no following page. It serves Grothendieck's 1986 'Ateliers' reflections on a tame or combinatorial geometry of figures and their decompositions.
errors: Index bookkeeping looks reversed or ambiguous. If the Y_j^0 (of F, index set J) are formed from the X_i^0 (of G, index set I), the coarse order on J should be deduced from the fine order on I by grouping (a quotient), not the order on I from that on J. As written, 'la relation d'ordre sur I ... se déduit ... de celle de J' is either a slip or uses I and J the other way round. The passage is crossed out anyway.
The thought is unfinished: the sentence is cut off and the page is cancelled.

ideas.what: Subdivision of a stratification/decomposition as a refinement whose strata group into the coarse strata, with the coarse incidence order being the quotient of the fine one (equivalently, the Alexandrov topology of the coarse poset is a quotient topology)
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of stratifications / subdivision; surjective quotient map of face (stratum) posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (PL topology and subdivision of complexes); in stratified-space theory, e.g. Whitney/Thom/Mather, and later refinements in exit-path ∞-categories (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratified structures in general terms; this specific formulation is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: A short, cancelled, unfinished paraphrase of a standard notion: subdivision as grouping of strata with the quotient incidence order. It adds nothing beyond the conditions on the previous page and contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The whole text is struck through by two diagonal lines, consistent with the [-...-] marking.
'(formés formés des X_i^0)' should read '(formés des X_i^0)': the image shows 'formés des X_i^0' once.
The last word is hard to read; it may be 'partition', 'partitionnement' or similar, ending in '...t...'. Treat it as uncertain.
The quotation marks around "autres formes" are visible in the image; reading the phrase as 'autres formes' is plausible but uncertain.
